newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr/yen spot/forward spread wider on Japan premium.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/yen spot/forward spread wider on Japan premium.

text.p: The spread between dollar/yen currency spot and forward rates widened recently as a result of the rising Japan premium, currency dealers said on Wednesday.

Dealers said Japanese banks, faced with an increase in the Japan premium -- the extra cost they are charged when raising funds in the Euro interbank market -- have turned to the dollar/yen forward market to raise dollar funds, and this added demand has caused the spread to expand.
Demand for dollar funds through the beginning of next year has been particularly strong, leading to a widening of the spread for that period, dealers added.

The spread between the spot rate and the forward rate for the period from December 30 to January 6, which covers the Japanese new year holidays, has widened to around 0.16 yen today from 0.13 yen a month ago.
Dealers said the recent rise in U.S. market interest rates was also contributing to the widening spot/forward spread.

The spread in part reflects the interest rate differential between Japan and the United States. The currency with the higher interest rate has a lower exchange rate in a forward contract than it does in the regular spot rate.

Dealers also said many Japanese banks had been holding off on raising dollars via forward contracts because they had expected U.S. market interest rates to soften, which would have led to a narrowing of the spread.

"Many banks were slow in raising dollars through forward contracts as they had expected U.S. interest rates to head lower in the face of weak U.S. economic indicators back in November," said a city bank dealer.
But the banks were forced to abandon this view, he said, when the U.S. bond market recently began a downward correction.
On Wednesday, the Japan premium remained high at over 40 basis points, due to foreign banks' reluctance to lend money ahead of the end-year book closing, money traders said.

The premium resurfaced in late November after debt-laden Hanwa Bank Ltd, a regional Japanese bank, was ordered to halt operations by regulators, raising concerns about the soundness of Japan's financial industry. -- George Nishiyama, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-5473-3710
